transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Evelyn Park (Redwood AE), Jonah Reed (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Velascale Partnerships), Leah Turner (Velascale Cloud Solutions), Priya Nair (Velascale Security)

[00:00] Evelyn Park: hey everyone thanks for joining— i think we've got about 45 minutes, um quick intros then we'll jump in. i'm evelyn, i'm on partnerships AE at redwood. jonah is our se who will cover technical stuff.
[00:18] Marco Diaz: thanks, evelyn. marco here, head of partnerships. leah handles cloud solutions, priya's on for security questions. nice to meet you.
[00:29] Jonah Reed: nice to meet you all. quick agenda, partner intro, our respective infra, where there's overlap, and then possible pilot flow.
[00:40] Leah Turner: sounds good, hit us— maybe start with the redwood offering high level.
[00:45] Evelyn Park: sure. high level redwood is an inference platform— hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and a private vpc/on prem option. we focus on predictable latency and cost controls, dev first apis, and tooling for rollouts. most partners we talk to are either cloud/GPU vendors looking to offer managed inference stacks or systems integrators who want a consistent runtime for customers.
[01:05] Marco Diaz: ok got it. at velascale we offer baremetal gpu pools, regionally distributed, and we do managed k8s for some customers. we're evaluating deeper partnerships to bundle inference as a service. big priority is security and easy onboarding.
[01:18] Priya Nair: ditto — for us SOC2 is table stakes and we need KMS integration and audit logs. we also care about data residency— some customers can't leave eu data centers.
[01:30] Jonah Reed: totally reasonable. on the private side redwood can run in your vpc or on-prem; we support KMS/HSM integrations and ship audit logs. small caveat: some early customers saw subtle naming mismatches in our auto transcripts, so we usually do a short validation step for compliance teams.
[01:52] Marco Diaz: naming mismatches? like speaker labels?
[01:55] Jonah Reed: yeah small transcription artifacts, but not security relevant— more like things we saw in speech-to-text exports. but the platform's logs and telemetry are robust.
[02:06] Leah Turner: performance— what does dedicated look like? our customers ask about throughput per GPU and latency SLOs.
[02:12] Evelyn Park: dedicated is reserved gpu pools with configurable autoscaling and burst. we publish perf profiles per model; typical numbers depend on model size/quantization. for example, a 7B quantized to 8-bit on A100-class infra we see median latencies in the 30–80ms per token range under continuous batching but that's workload dependent.
[02:34] Jonah Reed: we also do kv cache and prefix caching to improve tail latency for chat-style workloads; routing policies can steer critical traffic to lower-latency pools.
[02:45] Marco Diaz: okay that helps. customers care about the economics— how do you price dedicated vs hosted? and what's the split for a partner— arevenue share?
[02:55] Evelyn Park: hosted is usage-based per token; dedicated is monthly reserved capacity, typically a commit. for partnerships we have standard referral and co-sell models— details depend on ARR and go-to-market activity. we'll follow up with the partner one-pager and pricing sheet.
[03:10] Priya Nair: on the private deployment: integration with our identity stack is critical. we use SAML SSO, and we need RBAC controls. does redwood support SAML and fine-grained roles?
[03:20] Jonah Reed: yes we integrate with SAML/SSO, and have RBAC at route and model level. audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM. in private deployments customers can host control plane in their vpc or run air-gapped mode if needed.
[03:34] Leah Turner: regionally, can you pin model versions per region? eg eu uses different model variants for compliance.
[03:40] Evelyn Park: yes, deployment abstraction allows pinning by region/route. routing policies can fallback to compatible variants if preferred variant is unavailable.
[03:48] Marco Diaz: good. any concerns around compatibility with our infra? we run mostly on k8s, but some customers use proprietary provisioning.
[03:55] Jonah Reed: k8s is common, we have an operator for private deployment and terraform modules for infra. Some partners with custom provisioning required minor adaptors; we can scope during a tech-deep-dive.
[04:10] Marco Diaz: can you talk about model catalog and what models you certify?
[04:15] Evelyn Park: we curate open models and verify performance profiles; we also support private model uploads for customers in private deployments. certified models are ones we've profiled for latency/throughput and have optimized kernels.
[04:26] Marco Diaz: competition— who do you see as main competitors?
[04:29] Evelyn Park: there are infra folks like lambda labs for baremetal, model infra providers and managed apis like pinecone for vectors, and bigger cloud providers occasionally. mention of anthropic comes up for model access depending on use case.
[04:44] Leah Turner: curious about benchmarking— we'd want to run joint benchmarks to show Velascale hardware + redwood runtime. do you have a benchmark template?
[04:52] Jonah Reed: yes, i'll share a benchmark spreadsheet and sample perf numbers. typical pilot includes workload sampling from a target customer, a 2-week perf run, and QA checks for quality regressions.
[05:05] Marco Diaz: quality regressions— are you running evals against prompts? some customers are strict on hallucination rates.
[05:11] Evelyn Park: we run prompt sets/evals and have regression alerts tied to them. for pilots we can include regen checks and human eval samples.
[05:20] Priya Nair: encryption at rest and in transit? KMS integration specifics?
[05:24] Jonah Reed: encryption at rest via your cloud provider KMS or HSM; we support customer-managed keys in private deployments. in hosted mode we offer customer key support for enterprise plans.
[05:34] Leah Turner: any gotchas around KV cache and data leakage? some customers worried about cached prefixes containing PII.
[05:40] Jonah Reed: good point— cache controls let you choose retention policies; for regulated customers we recommend disabling long lived prefix caching or scoping cache per-tenant and ensuring encrypted storage.
[05:55] Marco Diaz: for GTM— we'd want joint case studies. our sales ops will want a clear referral flow and lead assignment.
[06:03] Evelyn Park: that's part of the partner one-pager; our partnerships ops will work with your sales ops.
[06:10] Leah Turner: let's talk timeline— Velascale has a list of enterprise customers who asked for integrated inference; we could do a pilot Q1. realistic?
[06:18] Evelyn Park: yes, a Q1 pilot is realistic. ideal sequence: NDA if needed, share infra diagrams, run tech deep-dive, then pilot quickstart (2–4 weeks).
[06:29] Marco Diaz: NDA — we already have a master NDA with some vendors, but i'll check.
[06:33] Priya Nair: required for our side too, mainly for sharing customer lists.
[06:37] Jonah Reed: ack — we can attach NDA to the follow up email.
[06:42] Evelyn Park: ok i can send partner one-pager and pricing. jonah will send the benchmark template. marco/priya please share infra diagram and list of top 3 target customers.
[06:55] Marco Diaz: will do. quick tech question — do you support model quantization recommendations and auto-tuning?
[07:01] Jonah Reed: yep — redwood optimize gives quantization and model/quant recommendations by workload. we also have kernel selection and compilation steps in the runtime to pick best kernels for your hardware profile.
[07:15] Leah Turner: for region-specific models, can we host different model artifacts in our EU region and still use your control plane?
[07:21] Jonah Reed: you can either host model artifacts in-region and connect to the control plane, or run fully private control plane in your region. both supported.
[07:31] Marco Diaz: pricing again— if we resell bundled infra+redwood, is there an MOQ or commit?
[07:36] Evelyn Park: for dedicated there's typically a monthly or annual commit. for co-sell models we can be flexible on pilot terms; larger rev-share contracts have minimums. we'll outline options in the follow-up.
[07:48] Priya Nair: security checklist items — SOC2 report, penetration test recents, encryption key options, audit log delivery method. can you send SOC2 and pentest summary?
[07:58] Jonah Reed: yes we'll include SOC2 summary and high level pen test report in the security pack. note some internal names in reports can be slightly off, we recommend a short security sync for clarifications.
[08:10] Evelyn Park: ok quick recap and next steps — i'll send partner one-pager, pricing sheet and schedule proposed deep-dive for 2026-01-20. jonah will attach benchmark template and sample perf numbers. marco/priya to share infra diagram and list of pilot customers. marco we'll check NDA status.
[08:30] Marco Diaz: sounds good, thanks all. excited to explore.
[08:34] Evelyn Park: thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email.
[08:38] (call ends)

Notes: transcript has occasional transcription artifacts (names spelled alia, redwood spelled reddwood in a few auto sections) — validated as medium quality. Links shared: partner-one-pager.pdf (sent after call), benchmark-template.xlsx (to be sent), SOC2-summary.pdf (to be sent).
